steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026.
The deadline is six days from today, which is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

On October 30, 2026:
*   Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 (as Daylight Saving Time ends on Oct 25).
*   Pacific Time will be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7 (as Daylight Saving Time ends on Nov 1).

The time difference is 8 hours (UTC+1 vs UTC-7). Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PDT.

Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM PDT on October 30:
11:59 PM PDT + 8 hours = 7:59 AM CET on October 31.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. "This coming Monday" is November 2, 2026.
On November 2, Los Angeles will be on PST (UTC-8), and Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).
Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles.
10:00 AM PST + 9 hours = 7:00 PM (19:00) CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts at 18:00 on October 24, 2026, in your local time (Madrid). Since it lasts exactly 48 hours, which is two full days, the end time will be the same hour two days later.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest submissions close exactly 72 hours after October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT, which is October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT.
On October 29, 2026, Pacific Time will still be on Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7), as US DST ends in November. Madrid, Spain, will be on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), as European DST ends on the last Sunday of October.
Therefore, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PDT (UTC+1 vs UTC-7).
Adding 8 hours to 10:00 AM PT on October 29, 2026, gives 6:00 PM (18:00) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The submission close time is October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.
Adding 36 hours to this time, the results announcement in ET will be on November 2, 2026, at 11:59 AM ET.
On November 2, 2026, Eastern Time (ET) will be Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5. Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
Therefore, Madrid time is 6 hours ahead of EST.
Adding 6 hours to 11:59 AM ET gives 05:59 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 converts to 2026-09-08 23:39:00 UTC. Tokyo is UTC+9, so adding 9 hours gives 2026-09-09 08:39:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2026-09-09 08:39

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2, at that date and time. The deadline is before the end of Daylight Saving Time on the last Sunday of October.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.
On October 25, 2026, Pacific Time will still be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7, as US Daylight Saving Time ends in November.
Madrid (Spain) will transition from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on October 25, 2026, at 03:00 local time. Therefore, by the time the deadline is reached, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

The deadline is 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026.
Convert to UTC: 23:59 PDT on Oct 25 = 06:59 UTC on October 26.
Convert to Madrid time (CET, UTC+1): 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 CET on October 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Here's how to determine the deadline:

1.  **US DST End Date 2026**: Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, November 1st is a Sunday, so DST ends on **November 1, 2026**.
2.  **Eastern Time on that day**: On November 1, 2026, clocks fall back from Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) to Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5) at 2:00 AM. Therefore, by 12:00 noon on that day, the Eastern Time zone will be operating as **EST (UTC-5)**.
3.  **Deadline in UTC**: 12:00 noon EST is 17:00 UTC (12:00 + 5 hours).
4.  **Lima Local Time**: Lima, Peru observes Peru Time (PET), which is **UTC-5** and does not observe Daylight Saving Time.
5.  **Conversion to Lima Time**: 17:00 UTC converted to PET (UTC-5) is 12:00 (17:00 - 5 hours).

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) refers to the latest possible time on Earth, which is typically UTC-12. "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is equivalent to January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12.

To convert this to UTC:
00:00 UTC-12 + 12 hours = 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2027.

Tokyo is UTC+9. To convert UTC to Tokyo time:
12:00 UTC + 9 hours = 21:00 JST on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney will be in Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), which is UTC+11. New York will be in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
To convert the deadline from Sydney time to New York time, we first convert Sydney time to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and then to New York time.

1.  **Sydney Time (AEDT):** October 5, 2026, 5:00 PM (17:00)
2.  **Convert to UTC:** AEDT is UTC+11, so subtract 11 hours from Sydney time.
    17:00 - 11 hours = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.
3.  **Convert to New York Time (EDT):** EDT is UTC-4, so subtract 4 hours from UTC.
    06:00 - 4 hours = 02:00 EDT on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
